title: Queries
hook: Quakers ask themselves regular questions about truth, peace, simplicity, equality

segments.voice: Yesterday, meeting for worship: Friends waiting on God in silence. Your line was expectant waiting.

Do I keep my word? Read a question like that aloud to a room of Friends, and then leave it there. Not a question about doctrine. A question about the people in the room. The silence holds it. Nobody raises a hand. Nobody is graded. Each person carries it inward and answers it there, or doesn't yet. Friends call these questions queries. Quaker meetings keep written sets of them, about truth, peace, simplicity and equality, and come back to them again and again.

Why questions instead of rules? A rule tells you what to do and lets you stop thinking once you've done it. A question keeps working on you. Friends use queries to search their own lives, not to check off a list. It's an old instinct in the Bible. Paul writes to the Corinthians: "Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves." And Lamentations says: "Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD." Queries gather around what Friends call testimonies, the shape their faith takes in daily life. Truth: Jesus said, "let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay," and Friends have tried to let a plain word be enough, without oaths. Peace: how do you meet conflict? Simplicity: what are you carrying that you don't need? Equality: how do you treat people, all of them? That last one has a root. George Fox, an early Quaker preacher, urged Friends to "walk cheerfully over the world, answering that of God in every one." Friends speak of that of God as a light in each person. To answer to it is to speak and act toward that light, even when the rest of the person is hard going. So a query on equality isn't really about manners. It's about whether you see that of God across the table. And a query isn't a test with a right answer. If you answer one quickly, it probably hasn't done its work yet.

Choose one of the four, truth, peace, simplicity or equality, and turn it into a plain question about your own week: where did I bend the truth, what am I holding that I don't need, whom did I treat as less? Don't rush to answer; let the question do the work. If you pray, hold it before God; if you don't, simply hold it honestly.
Queries. Questions Quakers ask themselves in meeting, about truth, peace, simplicity and equality, answered inwardly and never graded.
Your line: answer to that of God. There's a light in each person, even the hard ones. Until tomorrow.
